## Yes — the repo ships no agent context at all

`crimes_00011` / `missing_agent_context` — **Missing Agent Context**, medium severity, confidence 0.90:

```
no AGENTS.md found at repo root
no CLAUDE.md found at repo root
no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present
no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present
package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands
```

It's the only `universal`-pack agent-context finding in the report, and it's the one finding here that isn't about a specific line of code — it's about the repo as a whole. (The `file: assets/cjs_shims.js` anchor is just where the detector pinned a repo-level fact; don't read it as "the problem is in cjs_shims.js".)

## What this costs you on your first PR

The scan gives you a concrete picture of what an agent walks into blind:

- **It won't know how to build or test.** `package.json` declares two binaries (`tsup`, `tsup-node`) and there's a `test/` directory, but nothing tells an agent which script runs the suite, or that the tests shell out to real builds — `test/utils.ts` has fan-in 9 and does `fs.readFileSync` on build output (`crime_00067`). An agent will guess a command, guess wrong, and either report a false pass or churn.
- **It won't know which files are load-bearing.** `src/utils.ts` has fan-in 18, `src/plugin.ts` 10, `src/log.ts` 9 (`crime_00039`, `crime_00008`, `crime_00021`). All three are ordinary-looking modules. An agent asked to "clean up utils" will restructure a file 18 modules depend on, with no signal that it shouldn't.
- **The tests won't catch its mistakes.** 24 `weak_test_signal` findings — 12 tests with **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls (`crime_00052`–`crime_00063`), 12 more with only weak matchers. An agent that runs the suite and sees green has learned almost nothing. This is the compounding one: missing context plus a suite that can't refute a bad edit means confident-but-wrong changes land.
- **It will land edits inside 200–300-line functions it only partially read.** `build` is 293 lines, `runEsbuild` 237, `main` 153 (`crime_00023`, `crime_00022`, `crime_00006`). Without a note saying "these are known orchestrators, extract rather than extend," the default agent move is to add another branch.

Net effect: `agent_risk` on this finding is 0.47 — mid-pack, but it's a **multiplier** on the other 86. Every other finding gets more dangerous when nothing tells an agent the rules before it edits.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

The detector checks for an `AGENTS.md` at repo root, so a single file resolves it. Keep it short — this skeleton is deliberately the minimum that carries real information, not a docs project. Everything in `<angle brackets>` needs a human to fill in; I've grounded the rest in what the scan actually observed.

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Bundler powered by esbuild. Ships two binaries: `tsup` and `tsup-node`.

## Commands

- Install: `<pnpm install | npm ci>`
- Build: `<npm run build>`
- Test: `<npm test>` — integration tests that run real builds into temp dirs
  and assert on output files. Slow; run the whole suite before opening a PR.
- Typecheck / lint: `<npm run typecheck>` / `<npm run lint>`

## Layout

- `src/index.ts` — public API entry, `build()` orchestrator
- `src/cli-main.ts` — CLI entry (`main`)
- `src/esbuild/` — esbuild pipeline and plugins
- `src/rollup.ts`, `src/api-extractor.ts`, `src/tsc.ts` — .d.ts generation paths
- `test/` — integration tests; `test/utils.ts` is the shared harness

## Before you edit

These files are load-bearing — prefer additive changes, read the importers first:

- `src/utils.ts` (18 importers)
- `src/plugin.ts` (10 importers)
- `src/log.ts` (9 importers)
- `test/utils.ts` (9 importers) — changing the harness changes every test

## Conventions

- `build`, `buildAll`, `buildStart`, and `getRollupConfig` perform side effects
  (file removal, logging) despite read-like names. Don't assume purity.
- `src/index.ts:build` (~290 lines) and `src/esbuild/index.ts:runEsbuild` (~240)
  are known orchestrators. Extract helpers; don't add branches inline.
- Options are passed as a wide `options` bag (`runEsbuild` reads 38 distinct
  fields). Check `<Options type location>` before adding a field.

## Testing rules

Several existing tests run a build with no assertions. **Do not copy that
pattern.** Every new test must assert on observable output — emitted file
contents, exit code, or thrown error. A passing suite is not currently
strong evidence a change is correct.

## Don't

- Don't add a second package manager lockfile.
- Don't restructure the esbuild plugin ordering without <owner> review.
```

Two things to flag: the command block is the part that most needs a human — I'd be guessing at the exact scripts, and a wrong build command in an AGENTS.md is worse than none, because agents trust it. And the "Testing rules" section is the highest-value paragraph in the file; it's the only thing standing between an agent and the false confidence those 12 assertion-free tests hand out.

Re-run `crimes scan --format json` after adding it and `crime_00011` should drop out of the report.
